chapter_name: Retirement and Death of a Partner
learning_objective: 🎯 Figure out how to smoothly settle accounts, value shares, and calculate final payouts when a partner leaves the firm or passes away.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: When a partner leaves, their share of the profit is left behind. The remaining partners 'gain' this share. Gaining Ratio is the ratio in which the remaining partners acquire the retiring partner's share.
The retiring/deceased partner is entitled to their share of the firm's goodwill. The remaining partners must pay them this amount directly from their own capital accounts, in their Gaining Ratio.
If the firm doesn't have enough cash to pay the retiring partner immediately, the final amount owed is transferred to a 'Loan Account', which earns interest (usually 6% p.a.) until paid.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🕊️ Death of a Partner & Profit to Date
main_concepts.simple_explanation: If a partner dies mid-year, their family (Executors) gets their share of profit earned from the start of the year until the exact date of death. This is calculated using time or sales data and put in a 'P&L Suspense Account'.

fun_activity.title: ⏱️ The Mid-Year Math
fun_activity.instructions: Assume a partner dies on June 30th. The financial year started on April 1st. Count the exact number of months they were alive in the current financial year. (Answer: 3 months). Their interim profit will be calculated for just this 3/12 fraction of the year!

exam_tips: 📌 Formula: Gaining Ratio = New Ratio - Old Ratio. (Opposite of Admission!).

📌 P&L Suspense Account is only used if the profit-sharing ratio of the remaining partners DOES NOT change. If the new ratio changes, adjust the deceased partner's profit directly through the gaining partners' capital accounts.
📌 When preparing the Executor’s Account, make sure to add everything owed (Capital, Goodwill, Interest, Reserves, Share of Profit) before calculating final payment.
quick_recap: ⭐ Remaining partners compensate the outgoing partner for Goodwill in the Gaining Ratio.
⭐ Revaluation of assets and liabilities is done exactly the same way as in Admission.
⭐ An Executor is the legal representative who receives the deceased partner's dues.
